text_blocks.snippet: While technically, most foods contain at least some calories, some vegetables are so low in calories that they are often referred to as "zero-calorie" or "negative-calorie" foods. These vegetables are typically high in water and fiber, making them very low in calories while also promoting satiety.
Examples of vegetables often cited as having zero or very low calories:

list.title: Celery:
list.snippet: Celery is primarily composed of water and fiber, making it very low in calories.

list.title: Cucumber:
list.snippet: Similar to celery, cucumbers have a high water content and are very low in calories.

list.title: Lettuce:
list.snippet: Certain types of lettuce, like iceberg lettuce, are very low in calories.

list.title: Spinach:
list.snippet: Spinach is low in calories and packed with nutrients, including vitamins and minerals.

list.title: Broccoli:
list.snippet: Broccoli is a cruciferous vegetable low in calories and rich in vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants.

list.title: Cauliflower:
list.snippet: Cauliflower is another cruciferous vegetable that is low in calories and can be used as a low-carb substitute for other foods.

list.title: Bell peppers:
list.snippet: Bell peppers, particularly green ones, are low in calories and high in vitamin C.

list.title: Radishes:
list.snippet: Radishes are crunchy root vegetables with a slightly spicy taste and low calorie count.

list.title: Cabbage:
list.snippet: Cabbage, especially green and red varieties, is low in calories and packed with nutrients.

list.title: Calorie Density:
list.snippet: These vegetables are low in calorie density, meaning they provide few calories per unit of weight or volume.

list.title: Satiety:
list.snippet: Their high water and fiber content can help you feel full and satisfied, potentially aiding in weight management.

list.title: Overall Diet:
list.snippet: While these vegetables are beneficial, they should be part of a balanced diet that includes a variety of nutrient-rich foods.

text_blocks.snippet: Most vegetables are low in calories. Many vegetables, especially leafy greens like spinach and lettuce, have very few calories per serving. For example, 100 calories worth of spinach is about 14 cups, according to BODi. Other vegetables like bell peppers, mushrooms, and kale also offer a good amount of volume for 100 calories. Starchy vegetables like corn and potatoes contain more calories per serving.
snippet_highlighted_words: leafy greens like spinach and lettuce, have very few calories per serving

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at the calorie content of some common vegetables:
Low-Calorie Options (often under 20 calories per cup):

list.snippet: Arugula: 5 calories per cup.
Lettuce: 5 calories per cup.
Cucumber: 16 calories per cup.
Celery: 14 calories per cup.
Radishes: 19 calories per cup.
Spinach: Very low, with 14 cups making up 100 calories, according to BODi.
Mushrooms: 25 medium mushrooms are about 100 calories, according to BODi.

text_blocks.snippet: Other Vegetables (calorie counts vary by serving size and type):

list.snippet: Bell Peppers: 3 medium bell peppers are around 100 calories, according to BODi.
Brussels Sprouts: 13 sprouts are around 100 calories, according to BODi.
Kale: 13 cups are around 100 calories, according to BODi.
Asparagus: 32 medium spears are around 100 calories, according to BODi.
Broccoli: 5 cups of broccoli florets are around 100 calories, according to BODi.
Corn: ⅔ cup is around 100 calories, according to BODi.
Potatoes: ¾ small potato is around 100 calories, according to BODi.

list.title: Serving Size Matters:
list.snippet: Always pay attention to the serving size when looking at calorie information, according to BODi.

list.title: Cooking Methods:
list.snippet: Cooking methods can also impact calorie count. For example, adding oil or butter will increase the calories.
